place_fields.summary: A historic Shiva temple in Shahapur, Belagavi, revered as Dakshin Kashi. Sources describe a sacred swayambhu Shiva lingam, additional shrines, devotional murals and a temple tank.
place_fields.best_time: August to October and November to February

planning_attributes.description: Shri Kapileshwara Swamy Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva on Kaplieshwar Road in Shastri Nagar, Shahapur, Belagavi. It is described as one of Belagavi's oldest Shiva shrines and as Dakshin Kashi.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The temple is associated with an ancient Shiva shrine and is described by sources as dating to around 1000 CE or the late 12th century; its principal Shivling is regarded as swayambhu. It attracts large devotional crowds during Shravan Mondays and Maha Shivaratri.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: The temple is on Kaplieshwar Road in Shahapur, near the Shahpur flyover. Belagavi railway station and bus stand are nearby, and road access is available by local transport.
planning_attributes.notes: Sources describe parking for two-wheelers and four-wheelers, with crowding possible on weekends.

place_fields.summary: A hilltop fort overlooking Belagavi, also known as Yellurgad or Rajhansgad. It served as a strategic outpost and watchtower and contains a Shiva temple, an ancient well and fortifications with panoramic views.

planning_attributes.description: Yellur Fort, also called Yellurgad or Rajhansgad, stands on a hill near Belagavi and offers panoramic views of Belagavi city and surrounding agricultural areas. The fort has a main entrance, stone walls, an ancient well and a Shiva temple.
planning_attributes.elevation_or_height: Approximately 2,500 feet (762 metres) above sea level.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The fort was originally constructed by the Ratta dynasty and later renovated in stone by Asad Khan Lari of Bijapur. It served as an outpost of Belagavi Fort for spotting approaching enemies, and sources describe later control by the Yadavas, Hoysalas, Bahamanis, Adil Shahis and Marathas. During British rule, about 100 soldiers were posted there.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: The fort can be reached on foot or by road, with the road leading directly to the main entrance.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Published visitor timings are 06:00 AM to 07:00 PM.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The fort is on a hillock with changing levels and fort walls; visitors should remain within accessible areas and observe the published daytime visiting hours.
planning_attributes.notes: The site includes a Shiva temple and a well; sources also describe panoramic views and a hilltop setting.

place_fields.summary: A Durga temple built into the entrance of Belagavi Fort and maintained by the Indian Army. It is a small place of worship associated with the fort entrance and the Belagavi cantonment's military heritage.

planning_attributes.description: Shri Military Durga Devi Temple is a Hindu temple and tourist attraction at the Belgaum Fort entrance in Belagavi Fort Area, Karnataka.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The temple is built into one side of Belagavi Fort's entrance and is maintained by the Indian Army. Sources identify it as part of a group of military-maintained temples associated with the Maratha Light Infantry Regimental Centre and Belagavi cantonment.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: The temple is located at the Belgaum Fort entrance in Belagavi Fort Area, near Belagavi railway station.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The temple is at a fort entrance where traffic is regulated by Army personnel; visitors should follow on-site directions and access controls.
planning_attributes.notes: Published listings report daily opening hours of 08:00 AM to 08:00 PM.
